messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: GPU pool 'hotpath-eu' saturated — queue depth 12k, 429 spike to 48% in last 5m. Pager: @ryan_oncall — paging now.
ryan_oncall: on it. give me a brief — is this autoscaler or raw capacity exhaustion?
maya_sre: quick summary: autoscaler health shows worker-launch attempts failing (quota/softlimit) + tokenbucket precheck causing immediate 429s for routed requests. queue growth started ~3501230500, exponential since 3501233000.
alex_runtime: seeing this in runtime logs too: "ERROR kvcache: failed to allocate worker -> quota_exceeded" then lots of "rate_limited: token_bucket_exhausted tier=hotpath". snippet: ```ERROR 2026-03-15T10:12:03Z autoscaler: launch failed: quotaExceeded: GPU quota 20 -> attempted 32```
julia_support: cs is getting tickets — several enterprise customers report timeouts and degraded responses. one customer (acme-inc) reports 7k failed requests in last 10m.
sophia_prod: tagging severity P1. impact: multiple active customers in EU region, degrade to timeouts/429s on generation endpoints. exec notified.
ryan_oncall: put mitigation plan in place. priorities: 1) reduce 429s for existing customers 2) stop queue growth 3) bring fallback path up. suggestions?
maya_sre: immediate mitigations I can run now: bump token bucket refill rate on tier 'hotpath' to 2x, temporarily relax per-request token cost for short requests, and disable strict tier mapping introduced in last deploy.
alex_runtime: confirm last deploy (deploy-bot id=deploy-2026-03-15-09:58) changed rate-tier mapping config to punt heavy requests to hotpath by default. that combined with token cost calc change caused hotpool to be preferred and tokens drained faster.
liam_ops: we can also emergency-burst extra GPUs in eu via cloud console but that'll take ~6-8m to attach. should we do that?
ryan_oncall: do both — maya roll tokenbucket change now, liam request burst. alex prepare routing fallback so non-SLA customers are encouraged to lower tier or queue.
maya_sre: running change now — showing command: ```kubectl apply -f - <<'YAML'
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
data:
  token_refill_rate: "200" # doubled from 100
  token_cost_short_request: "1" # was 3
  tier_mapping: "legacy" # revert to pre-deploy mapping
YAML```
maya_sre: applied. waiting for agents to pick up config. patch propagated to 6/8 nodes.
alex_runtime: routing flag ready: new route flag "prefer-hotpath=false" can be toggled at edge. I'll flip soft route for non-enterprise customers to prefer-warmpool. doing: ```curl -X POST https://edge-api/_flags -d '{"prefer-hotpath":false, "target":"nonprod,trial"}'```
deploy-bot: rollout started for edge-flag-change -> 3 regions.
ryan_oncall: liam, please request 8 extra gpus in eu-hotpool. label as emergency, attach to dedicated pool.
liam_ops: requested +8 gpus, cloud accepted, ETA attach 7m. also bumped worker launch retries to immediate (was backoff 30s) to speed up.
julia_support: telling CS team: "We are mitigating a capacity issue in EU. Some customers may see 429s for ~10-20m. We'll update with timeline."
sophia_prod: need count: how many customers are hitting 429s vs degraded latency? maya, can you pull metrics?
maya_sre: quick numbers via dashboard: unique API keys returning >5% 429 in last 10m = 14 keys (3 enterprise, 11 self-serve). aggregate token loss due to bucket exhaustion ~1.6M tokens/min. queue depth down from 12k -> 6.2k after initial token changes and routing flip. 429 rate dropped from 48% -> 22%.
alex_runtime: added temporary fallback: any request hitting hotpath 429 will now be automatically retried once to warmpool with downgraded model (gpt-medium) to preserve throughput. configured TTL 60s.
ryan_oncall: that retry sounds good. we must watch quality regression alerts. sophia coordinate with product/CS on messaging.
sophia_prod: drafting note: "We experienced capacity-related throttling in EU. We mitigated by routing lower-priority traffic to alternate pools and temporarily increasing capacity. Some requests may have returned lower-quality models; impact limited to non-enterprise traffic." will post to status after confirmation.
maya_sre: autoscaler health: restart recommended — I'm going to soft-restart autoscaler process to pick new config and clear launch locks. command: `systemctl restart redwood-autoscaler` -> doing it now.
alex_runtime: logs look cleaner: fewer "token_bucket_exhausted" after change. a couple of nodes report "stale-watch: lockfile present" — those cleared after restart.
liam_ops: cloud reports GPUs attached. hotpool capacity +8 live. queue depth trending down to ~1.3k. 429s down to 6% in EU.
julia_support: customers on SLA: acme-inc still saw 1.2k failed requests, CS is offering incident follow-up. Sophia, can you flag for postmortem?
sophia_prod: flagged. I'll own postmortem. include: root cause = rate-tier mapping change + token cost reduction -> tokenbucket underprovisioned for promotion policy; contributing = autoscaler launch failures due to quota/backoff; mitigations = tokenbucket refill increase, routing fallback, emergency capacity, autoscaler restart.
ryan_oncall: good. next actions: (1) undo the risky mapping deploy in canary, (2) run a tokenbucket capacity calc per traffic mix, (3) permanent fix for autoscaler quota handling (avoid immediate fail on quota and allow queued launches), (4) customer comms. assign owners?
maya_sre: I'll run tokenbucket calc and PR recommended defaults.
alex_runtime: I'll revert mapping change in next patch and add a feature-flag gate.
sophia_prod: I'll lead customer comms and postmortem.
liam_ops: I'll follow up with cloud quota team to get permanent quota increase for EU hotpool.
ryan_oncall: thanks all. current status: mitigations applied, queue draining, monitoring. keep the thread updated for 30m. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: deploy-2026-03-15-09:58 -> rollback requested by alex_runtime at 3501234569.
ryan_oncall: closing active pager escalation. keep channel open for postmortem notes.
summary: P1 incident — EU hotpool GPU saturation caused by token bucket/tier mapping change + autoscaler launch failures. Mitigations: tokenbucket refill increase, routing fallback, emergency capacity + autoscaler restart.
